title: Customs brokers demonstrate in Ouagadougou over licensing requirements
scope: One demonstration reported in Ouagadougou; wider coordination or continuation is not established.

title.summary: LeFaso reports a demonstration by customs brokers following deactivation of their Sydonia access.

start_date.summary: The article says the brokers demonstrated on 2 February 2021.

end_date.summary: No ending time, later continuation or resolution date is reported.

location.summary: The article locates the demonstration in Ouagadougou.

scope.summary: The report describes the brokers’ local demonstration, with no evidence it was a citywide or national event.

organizer.summary: Customs brokers are described as demonstrators; a spokesperson is quoted, while a formal organizer is not named in the saved report summary.

demands.summary: The spokesperson sought another delay to meet guarantee and credit requirements. Those are regulatory compliance conditions; no controlled category is assigned because the list does not clearly cover a licensing deadline.

participants.summary: The article describes several brokers, without a numerical count; its approximately 400 figure concerns affected firms, not demonstrators.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither the word several nor the count of affected firms establishes the number of people at the demonstration.

state_response.summary: Customs officials explicitly said the requirements would not be postponed again; other response dimensions are not established.

state_accommodation.summary: No accommodation: officials explicitly said the requirements would not be postponed again.

state_ignore.summary: Whether officials ignored the demonstration is not established; the article reports a direct customs response.

notes: The article says Sydonia access was disabled on 1 February; brokers sought time to comply with a guarantee and credit regime reportedly grounded in a UEMOA regulation and national order. open_questions: Were the disputed compliance requirements implemented as a national policy or only as enforcement of the regional UEMOA rule?
Did the demonstration continue after 2 February or end that day?
